gap: No retrieved work defines or reports an explicit held-out-hop transfer protocol (train on shallow-hop questions, evaluate on deeper-hop questions never seen at that depth) as a primary result, despite benchmarks being hop-stratified (MetaQA has 1/2/3-hop splits; CWQ requires up to 4-hop reasoning). The idea's central 'transfer to deeper multi-hop queries' claim therefore has no comparable published baseline or pre-registered protocol.

evidence.quote: MetaQA [38] contains more than 400k single and multi-hop (up to 3-hop) questions in the domain of movie, containing three datasets, namely MetaQA-1hop, MetaQA-2hop and MetaQA-3hop.
Complex WebQuestions 1.1 (CWQ) [32] is generated from WebQuestionsSP by extending the question entities or adding constraints to answers.

why_unaddressed: Papers report per-benchmark or per-hop-level results but train and test within the same hop distribution; none holds out a depth as a transfer target. Multi-hop QA generalization work (e.g. length-generalization studies) was not surfaced by the searched queries, so this remains an unverified gap requiring a targeted search.
research_question: Does context-enriched supervision improve accuracy on deeper-hop questions that were never trained at that depth, under a pre-registered held-out-hop split, relative to isolated-triple supervision and to training on all depths?
potential_experiment: Construct a strict hop-controlled split on MetaQA (train on 1-hop and 2-hop, test on 3-hop) and a cross-depth split for CWQ by depth annotation; report transfer accuracy alongside in-depth accuracy, and compare against the same model trained on all depths. Pre-register the split and report the context-vs-isolated contrast on it, plus a random-label and hop-lexical-cue control to rule out shortcut learning.
verification_required: Search for hop-length generalization / compositional generalization protocols in KGQA and multi-hop reasoning; verify whether a standard hop-transfer split already exists before creating a new one.
